note: Terms used by the lunar time and frame modules, each with its status and source. 'to confirm' marks a detail not read from the defining document.

terms.definition: Coordinate time of the Barycentric Celestial Reference System.
terms.source: IAU 1991 Resolution A4; IAU 2006 Resolution B3 (TDB)

terms.definition: Coordinate time of the Geocentric Celestial Reference System; TT runs at 1 - L_G against it.
terms.source: IAU 1991 Resolution A4; IAU 2000 Resolution B1.9

terms.definition: Time scale differing from TCG by the constant rate L_G = 6.969290134e-10.
Linear function of TCB: TDB = TCB - L_B (JD_TCB - T0) 86400 + TDB0, L_B = 1.550519768e-8, TDB0 = -6.55e-5 s.
Celestial reference system centred on the Moon, the lunar counterpart of the GCRS.
Coordinate time of the LCRS. In kshana, TCB - TCL is integrated from the first post-Newtonian rate at the Moon's centre; the origin convention is to confirm.
terms.source: IAU 2024 Resolution II (origin convention to confirm)

terms.definition: A lunar time standard under development. In kshana, LTC names the lunar-surface time model of src/lunar_time.rs with a stated origin, not an adopted standard.
terms.source: US OSTP policy memorandum, April 2024 (to confirm); src/lunar_time.rs

terms.definition: Mean rate of TCB against TCG, 1.48082686741e-8; recomputed at the geocentre as the check of the lunar rate.
Mean rate of TCB against TCL, computed by kshana from truncated ephemerides with a stated bound; not a defining constant.
Lunar body-fixed frame with the prime meridian toward the mean Earth direction and z along the mean rotation axis.
terms.source: IAU WGCCRE 2015 report (Archinal et al. 2018); NAIF moon_080317.tf

terms.definition: Lunar body-fixed frame along the Moon's principal axes of inertia, as realised by a JPL ephemeris (DE421, DE440).
The frame JPL DE430 Table 7 uses for the retroreflector coordinates; the ME convention.

A lunar terrestrial-type reference frame under international development. In kshana a named frame with ME axes (to confirm) realised by a stated 7-parameter datum; the default realisation is a zero-datum placeholder.
terms.source: definition and realisation parameters to confirm

terms.definition: The NASA, ESA and JAXA signal standard for the Augmented Forward Signal, Volume A, V1.0 of 29 January 2025.
The LunaNet navigation broadcast at 2492.028 MHz with a BPSK(1) data channel and a BPSK(5) pilot.
The service that broadcasts the AFS.
A proposed exchange format for lunar navigation data; no published content was found, so kshana has no LUNEX parser.
terms.source: IGS RINEX Committee, Cislunar PNT Workshop, February 2026 (format content not published)
